reports.title: Medtronic reports second quarter fiscal 2027 results; performance reflects consistent execution across the portfolio

guidance.heading: Guidance
section: The company today reiterated its FY27 organic revenue growth and EPS guidance. The company continues to expect FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of 7.25% to 7.75% and diluted non-GAAP EPS guidance of $5.94 to $6.00. The company is maintaining these ranges while absorbing the impact of the Diabetes business separation. This EPS guidance includes an estimated neutral impact from foreign currency exchange based on recent rates.

“Our priority is to continue converting the momentum in our businesses into strong financial performance,” said Thierry Piéton, chief financial officer. “We are investing behind our highest-priority growth opportunities while maintaining a disciplined focus on productivity and efficiency. That approach supports our objectives for sustainable growth, margin expansion and long-term shareholder value.”

desk.headline: Revenue up 4.5% to $9.36bn, below estimates; adjusted EPS of $1.34 in line; FY27 outlook reaffirmed after Diabetes split-off
results: Revenue rose 4.5% to $9.36bn (6.5% organic), short of the $9.48bn estimate; Diabetes was only included until its 15 October split-off.
Adjusted EPS of $1.34 was in line with the $1.33 estimate but 1.5% below last year's $1.36; GAAP EPS of $2.20 includes a $2.0bn gain on the MiniMed separation.
Cardiovascular led with 10.4% organic growth; cardiac ablation sales rose 58%, with 80% growth in the US.
Neuromodulation fell 2.2% organically and interventional cardiology was flat; adjusted operating margin slipped to 23.4% from 24.1%.
Half-year free cash flow was $2.6bn, up from $1.0bn; Medtronic plans to buy Contego Medical.

guidance.summary: Medtronic kept its FY27 outlook of 7.25–7.75% organic revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $5.94–6.00, absorbing the loss of the Diabetes business.

points: CEO Geoff Martha said the Affera heart-ablation platform keeps gaining share, adding about seven points in the US.
For Q3, management guided to about 5% organic growth and adjusted EPS of $1.40–1.42, calling it the hardest quarter seasonally.
The Hugo surgical robot won new FDA clearances; the target is over 250 installs worldwide by year-end.
Renal denervation now has a reimbursement code, but management said growth has not yet picked up.
CFO Thierry Piéton flagged a higher-than-expected tax rate in Q2 and said FY28 guidance will come in May.

watch: Whether ablation growth holds up against tougher comparisons in the second half.
Weak spots in neuromodulation, structural heart and China price controls.
The 10–11 December investor day for longer-term targets after the Diabetes exit.
